note: Two-class data model (closes #6). `Note` owns one record's lifecycle: serialization (insertion-order matching the existing on-disk layout), the SHA-256 checksum over CHECKSUM_FIELDS, and three-state `verify()` returning 'valid' / 'tampered' / 'no_checksum'. The third state exists because 24 of 25 pre-existing corpus entries predate checksums; collapsing to a binary tamper/no-tamper would have spammed warnings on every consult. `NotesStore` owns the corpus: `$WHY_NOTES_DIR`/git-root/cwd resolution, UUID indexing via `iter_notes`, primary lookup by repo+file, and `add_backlink` (the previously-loose `_backlink` helper). `related` is deliberately outside CHECKSUM_FIELDS so backlink writes do not invalidate integrity — verified by smoke test. The split mirrors actual ownership: a Note knows itself; a NotesStore knows where Notes live and how to find each other. A single combined class would force every Note instance to carry corpus-root state it does not need.
